Hireboard: building a Laravel + Next.js app from scratch with SDD Kit

This is a worked example of SDD Kit v3.1.0 (the 3.x line) used on a real-sized project. It starts from an empty folder and ends with a small job board, Hireboard, run by a team. Every step goes through the kit's single front door, /sdd. Twelve chapters take eleven tickets (HIRE-1 to HIRE-11) through the route the kit picks for each one.

Hireboard, its people (Maya Chen, product owner; Alex Rivera, developer) and the timeline (2026-10-19 to 2026-11-03) are fictional. Agent output in the chapters is simulated: it is abridged and labelled as simulated. The commands, flags, workflow arguments and file paths are the kit's real ones. The code under artifacts/ is complete, and has been compiled and tested (see Artifacts).

Choose a host

The product, tickets, specifications and acceptance criteria are shared. Each chapter has a concrete Codex path before its original Claude Code narrative. Simulated outputs retain their original context; they are not live acceptance evidence for either host.

Start here Claude Code Codex
Install Claude guide Codex guide, from a checkout containing the adapter
Route a ticket /sdd-kit:sdd HIRE-3 (plugin), /sdd HIRE-3 (file-copy) $sdd HIRE-3
Follow a workflow /workflows $progress, retaining the native run id
Project context CLAUDE.md imports shared AGENTS.md Shared AGENTS.md plus explicitly read repository rules

Do not pin v3.1.0 expecting Codex support: it is the original Claude distribution baseline. Complete a running workflow before changing host or plugin build; a spec can be shared, but live worker ownership and stack/hook trust do not transfer.

What Hireboard is

A small job board with a Laravel 12 JSON API (repo api/) and a Next.js 15 App Router frontend (repo web/). The two repos sit in a parent-folder workspace with no git of its own (docs/multi-repo.md).

Who Can do
Visitor Search open job postings by keyword, location, remote and employment type. Open a job and the company's careers page. Read approved company reviews.
Candidate Register, keep a private profile, apply to open jobs (once per job), review a company (once per company).
Employer Register together with their company and see the applications to that company's jobs.
Admin (seeded) Approve or reject every review before it goes public.

The browser never holds the API token. The Next.js server keeps it in an HttpOnly cookie and calls the API for the browser. Chapter 03 makes that decision and records it as ADR-0001.

Who this is for

  • Developers new to the kit who want to see each /sdd route in context before using it on their own project. Read the chapters in order.
  • Developers already using the kit who want the exact arguments for a situation they are in, such as split repos, resuming a spec, or a bug with behavior that must not change. Jump to the chapter in the route map.
  • Leads setting up team practice. Read chapter 11.

You should be comfortable with Laravel and Next.js. The walkthrough explains the kit, not the frameworks.

Prerequisites

The full list with a version check is in 00 — Prerequisites. In short:

  • Claude Code or a plugin-capable Codex host, git and jq (INSTALLATION.md#prerequisites)
  • PHP 8.3 with Composer 2, and SQLite
  • Node.js 20 or newer
  • The kit installed for the selected host; Claude file-copy mode is used only after chapter 02 has scaffolded the repos (chapter 01 explains why)
  • Optional: gh for opening the pull requests

If you have never run the kit, do GETTING-STARTED.md first. For a one-paragraph version of each route, see USAGE-EXAMPLES.md.

Chapters

# Chapter In one line
00 Overview and prerequisites What you will build, the route map, toolchain check, how to read artifacts/.
01 Workspace and kit install Create the git-less workspace, install the kit without touching the not-yet-existing repos, write shared workspace instructions and the product brief.
02 New app: greenfield-build (HIRE-1) One workflow scaffolds both repos with CI and ships the first slice: search open jobs and open one.
03 Decision: SPA auth ADR (HIRE-2) tech-research compares four auth options against weighted criteria and writes ADR-0001, which Maya signs off.
04 Accounts and roles (HIRE-3) The feature pipeline end to end: write-spec, approval in /sdd, ship-feature with split-repo arguments, one PR per repo.
05 Company reviews, the M spec in full (HIRE-4) Every spec section, the clarity gate resolving six questions, then ship-feature building it.
06 Candidate profiles with /execute-task (HIRE-5) Approve only, build task by task with TDD, stop for the day, resume with --continue.
07 Job applications and /deep-review (HIRE-6) ship-feature, then an adversarial review before merge finds a race condition, which is fixed and re-reviewed.
08 Careers page S spec and a trivial change (HIRE-7, HIRE-8) The kit scaling down: a web-only S spec, and a copy-sized change with no spec at all.
09 Bug: closed jobs by direct link (HIRE-9) fix-bug with a mustNotChange list: reproduce, root cause, red regression test, guard tests, minimal fix.
10 QA plan and docs for shipped code (HIRE-10) qa-and-docs over the browse journey, which grew across four tickets and no single spec covers.
11 Running it as a team Contract-sync in CI, report-only routines, a project eval case, a pinned team marketplace, and HIRE-11 as an exercise.

Route map

/sdd sorts each request into one of six routes and launches exactly one pipeline (sdd SKILL.md). Each route appears at least once:

/sdd route Pipeline Chapter(s) Ticket(s)
new app greenfield-build workflow 02 HIRE-1
decision tech-research workflow, then an ADR 03 HIRE-2
feature /write-spec, human approval, ship-feature workflow 04, 05, 07, 08 HIRE-3, HIRE-4, HIRE-6, HIRE-7
feature (task by task) /write-spec, "Approve only", /execute-task 06 HIRE-5
trivial /simple-task, no spec 08 (also the review fix in 07) HIRE-8
bug fix-bug workflow with mustNotChange 09 HIRE-9
shipped qa-and-docs workflow 10 HIRE-10

Artifacts

Every file the walkthrough produces is in artifacts/, laid out by destination:

In this folder In your workspace
artifacts/workspace/ ~/work/hireboard/ (root CLAUDE.md and product-brief.md)
artifacts/api/ ~/work/hireboard/api/, a fresh Laravel 12 app after the scaffold commands in chapter 02
artifacts/web/ ~/work/hireboard/web/, a fresh create-next-app@15 app after the scaffold commands in chapter 02
artifacts/kit-fork/ a fork of the SDD Kit repo (the eval case in chapter 11)

What is in each repo folder:

  • Code. Application code, migrations, factories, seeders and tests in api/. App Router pages, Server Actions, components, typed API client and types in web/. CI workflows in both.
  • Project context. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md per repo, plus api/docs/ (architecture, business rules, API contract, schema docs, ADR-0001).
  • Kit records. Specs in api/.ai/specs/ (HIRE-3 to HIRE-6) and web/.ai/specs/ (HIRE-7), the /execute-task state and a verification report in api/.ai/, the /deep-review report in api/.ai/reviews/, and the QA plan and docs in web/docs/.

Three rules for reading them:

  1. Each file belongs to the chapter that first creates it, and shows its end-of-walkthrough state. A later change to it appears in the later chapter as a diff (for example, the HIRE-8 salary format in web/components/job-card.tsx).
  2. Files that grow with each feature (web/lib/api/endpoints.ts, api/docs/api/api-contracts.md, api/docs/context/business-rules.md, api/bootstrap/app.php, RepositoryServiceProvider, CompanyRepository, DatabaseSeeder and the workspace CLAUDE.md) already contain entries from later chapters.
  3. composer.json and package.json are not included. Dependencies come from the scaffold commands in chapter 02.

Compiled and tested. The full artifact set was dropped onto fresh scaffolds (Laravel Framework 12.70 with Pest 3.8 on PHP 8.3, and Next.js 15.5) and both repos pass every kit gate:

Repo Gate Result
api ./vendor/bin/pint --test pass
api ./vendor/bin/phpstan analyse --no-progress (level 5) pass, no errors
api php artisan test pass, 57 tests
web npm run lint pass
web npx tsc --noEmit pass
web npm test (Vitest) pass, 3 tests
web npm run build pass, 14 routes

To reproduce it, run the scaffold commands from chapter 02, copy artifacts/api/ and artifacts/web/ over the two fresh apps, run php artisan migrate:fresh --seed in api/, and run the gates above. The demo accounts all use the password password: candidate@hireboard.test, employer@acme.test and admin@hireboard.test.
